title: The Anonymous Project
excerpt: A white cube on stage where artists perform in total anonymity — a special visual commission for Le Guess Who? 2023.
description:
For Le Guess Who? 2023 I was commissioned to build the visual work that wraps the cube — a five-sided projection map driven by five projectors, playing three different kinds of material across its faces.
The first was a live point cloud: three depth cameras stayed inside the cube and streamed the performance out through TouchDesigner, so the room could watch what was happening within without ever seeing a face. The second was my first work with generative imagery — a model I trained to sit across the five sides of the cube, its stills upscaled by a second model. The third was volumetric 3D, built in TouchDesigner and run over the cube's geometry. Everything was played out live from Resolume.
> The Anonymous Project is a stage where artists perform inside a white cube, remaining anonymous at all times — before, during and after the performance. Audiences meet the work free of reputation or expectation, focused purely on the sound.
> So the cube had to show and conceal at once. What the audience saw was the performance rendered back onto its own walls as drifting points of light — the shape of someone playing, breathing with the music, never a face. Presence without identity.
credits: Commissioned by Le Guess Who? 2023. Concept, visual system & live operation: Jaco Schilp. Five-projector cube mapping; real-time point cloud from three Kinect depth cameras streamed through TouchDesigner; custom-trained image model with AI upscaling; volumetric 3D in TouchDesigner; live playback in Resolume. Photography: Ward Mevis.
